content: The relationship between household crowding and sleep duration was explored in certain analyses, as reported by Chambers in 2016. Johnson (2015) also contributed to this area of research. Evidence regarding drug and alcohol abuse was rated as low quality, based on findings from a cross-sectional study conducted by Al-Hemiary in 2015. This study involved 2,678 youths in Iraq and examined the impact of living conditions, such as having two or more individuals per room, on substance abuse and related outcomes. The study's findings were considered direct but imprecise due to limitations in the data.
